findings.claim: 08.07 contradicts itself on whether the overdub round-trip calibration blocks tracking: one row calls calibration 'a pre-flight gate item', another states pre-flight is 'Not a gate'. Nothing reconciles them, and the consequence of guessing wrong is that every take is silently mis-aligned by 5-25 ms.
findings.evidence: 08.07-overdub-mode.md:240 — edge row 'Player's local round-trip uncompensated or miscalibrated', User Sees column: "Calibration is a pre-flight gate item; residual + uncertainty shown per pass. A high residual is flagged, never hidden."  ||  08.07-overdub-mode.md:280 — request-lifecycle state 'Pre-flight': "Overdub checklist: disk, sample rate, monitoring path, round-trip calibration. Not a gate (08.06 D-05) — but a skipped calibration is stated, never blank."  ||  08.07-overdub-mode.md:303 — Stale state: "A stale calibration must never silently become the alignment offset."  ||  08.06-session-preflight-rig-readiness.md:113 — "D-05 | Pre-flight informs and records; it does not block".
findings.forcedInvention: Whether an overdub player whose round-trip calibration is absent, failed or stale may begin recording passes. Implementer A blocks the Recording state until calibration succeeds (per 'gate item' + the D-05-consistent statement at line 303 that a stale calibration must never become the offset). Implementer B lets them record with a 'calibration skipped' label (per 'Not a gate (08.06 D-05)'). The two products differ in whether a whole session's passes can be produced with no usable alignment offset.
